# Fantasy Playoff Weeks 19 to 21 (Ending 2027-03-28)

**Summary.** Our fantasy playoffs are weeks 19, 20 and 21, ending 2027-03-28. When you draft, the only schedule factor that matters is a two-game week inside those three weeks, and even that only breaks ties between similar players at the top of the auction. Schedule work belongs to the season: trade for playoff games before the 2027-03-04 deadline, then stream hard during the playoffs.

## Our dates and why they fit

Check your league settings and playoff dates before you look at any schedule. Ours are weeks 19, 20 and 21, and the season ends Sunday 2027-03-28. That date is matchup 21 in a standard 3-week playoff, which is the setup the experts recommend. ([08-16](https://youtu.be/gf_6GveiAls?t=88), [08-16](https://youtu.be/gf_6GveiAls?t=435))

Many experts now recommend March 28 as the end date. Yahoo's default is April 4. When a schedule note or game count gives both versions, use the March 28 one. Most public game counts are built on March 28 anyway. ([10-04](https://youtu.be/tnzmsYUA4yQ?t=2029), [10-03](https://youtu.be/_O9pc_u5vH0?t=1877), [09-29](https://youtu.be/sf6Ga9k-r-Q?t=1670), [09-29](https://youtu.be/XSPJL_mlFXo?t=1906), [09-29](https://youtu.be/NmdNvAz08oE?t=1822), [09-28](https://youtu.be/3Qm5wLjhvTw?t=2054))

The reason is the lottery reform and the tanking rule changes. Experts expect less resting late in the season, so late March games should be more competitive. One expert moved his own end date from March 21 to March 28 for this reason. Last season about eight or nine teams were tanking or resting players. Experts expect this season's fantasy playoffs to be less extreme, but that is a forecast, not a promise. ([10-01](https://youtu.be/aLP080hxizA?t=1964), [09-25](https://youtu.be/4gw4W4RTolY?t=1733), [08-16](https://youtu.be/gf_6GveiAls?t=372), [09-21](https://youtu.be/egRrai3Ax38?t=2141), [07-14](https://youtu.be/xHRF06_E9HE?t=144))

## Two-game weeks are the factor that matters

The one schedule factor that really matters is a two-game week during weeks 19, 20 or 21. In a head-to-head league like ours, a player whose team plays only twice in a playoff week gives you very little in that matchup. If you set aside teams with two-game playoff weeks, the schedules are mostly comparable and should not change player values much. ([08-16](https://youtu.be/gf_6GveiAls?t=1286), [08-16](https://youtu.be/gf_6GveiAls?t=1665), [09-28](https://youtu.be/3Qm5wLjhvTw?t=2054))

Do not worry about small differences in total playoff games. Twelve against eleven games is not worth the stress, because too much can change between October and March. ([08-16](https://youtu.be/gf_6GveiAls?t=1958))

Some two-game weeks are hard to avoid. One expert notes that Minnesota has a two-game week in the middle of the fantasy playoffs whatever weeks a head-to-head league uses. ([08-19](https://youtu.be/2mxpEpGU3H8?t=1933))

A two-game week early in the playoffs hurts less if your bracket gives top seeds a bye. A top-two seed with a first-round bye can absorb a week 19 two-game week. Check whether our playoff format has byes before you count on this. ([08-16](https://youtu.be/gf_6GveiAls?t=1361))

## At the auction: a tiebreaker, mostly for early picks

On 2026-10-18, use the playoff schedule only to break ties between two similar players. It is the least important factor at draft time. Never pay more for a worse player because he has a better playoff schedule. If two similar stars are nominated, the one with a two-game playoff week can be bid a little lower. Do not let the schedule drive your draft plan. ([10-01](https://youtu.be/aLP080hxizA?t=1978), [09-22](https://youtu.be/QbdrhJd7LiA?t=1983), [08-19](https://youtu.be/J1Eg3uaAICU?t=416), [08-19](https://youtu.be/2mxpEpGU3H8?t=1942), [08-16](https://youtu.be/gf_6GveiAls?t=150))

Apply this only to your most expensive players. In snake terms, experts say schedule quirks matter only for your first three rounds. In our 12-team league that is roughly the top 36 players, so in the auction it means your first few big purchases. The worry is your best player having a two-game week in the semifinals or the final. For mid-priced and cheap players, ignore the schedule. This applies most of all to the late flyers that make up the rest of our 144 drafted players. ([09-29](https://youtu.be/NmdNvAz08oE?t=1848), [09-29](https://youtu.be/NmdNvAz08oE?t=1879), [08-16](https://youtu.be/gf_6GveiAls?t=1797))

Player value is too uncertain to build around game counts. Players picked around 100 often finish around 30, and players picked around 20 can finish around 60. If a top player with a two-game playoff week stays cheap late in the bidding and no better option is left, buy him. Just do not reach for him early. ([08-16](https://youtu.be/gf_6GveiAls?t=187), [08-16](https://youtu.be/gf_6GveiAls?t=1522))

Having up to about three players from one NBA team is fine. It is more acceptable if that team has no two-game weeks in weeks 19 to 21. Five from one team is too many, because one bad playoff week would then hit a large part of your lineup. ([09-25](https://youtu.be/4gw4W4RTolY?t=364))

The experts differ on how hard to apply the penalty. One view is that a two-game playoff week should drop a player down your board in any head-to-head league. The other is that it should only move him down a little, and only when he is tied with a similar player, never across a clear talent gap. For our auction, follow the softer view at the top of the board. Use the harder view only when the price gap between two similar players is small. ([08-16](https://youtu.be/gf_6GveiAls?t=1665), [08-19](https://youtu.be/2mxpEpGU3H8?t=1942), [08-19](https://youtu.be/J1Eg3uaAICU?t=416), [08-16](https://youtu.be/gf_6GveiAls?t=150))

## During the season: trades before 2027-03-04

Schedule improvements are worth doing as the season goes on, not at the draft. The season has three phases: discovery early, optimizing in the middle, and maximizing near the end and in the playoffs. Use the middle phase to fix your playoff schedule through trades. ([09-01](https://youtu.be/skKXe2CRl8Q?t=1408), [09-01](https://youtu.be/skKXe2CRl8Q?t=1712))

Our trade deadline is 2027-03-04, before week 19 starts. Check by then which of your key players have a two-game week in weeks 19 to 21. Look for even trades where you send one out for a similar player with more playoff games. Judge a team's playoff schedule by its playoff week game counts and by its back-to-backs inside those weeks. Back-to-backs during the fantasy playoffs matter more than the season total. ([09-01](https://youtu.be/skKXe2CRl8Q?t=1408), [09-29](https://youtu.be/XSPJL_mlFXo?t=1906), [08-16](https://youtu.be/gf_6GveiAls?t=893), [08-16](https://youtu.be/gf_6GveiAls?t=1286))

## During the playoffs: stream for games

In weeks 19 to 21, maximize games. Drop stashed or injured players who will not help in time, and stream as much as you can. Smart streaming and avoiding two-game weeks are how the playoff schedule matters later in the season. Our limit is 6 acquisitions per week with daily FAB processing, so plan the adds around the days with the most games. ([09-01](https://youtu.be/skKXe2CRl8Q?t=1712), [09-22](https://youtu.be/QbdrhJd7LiA?t=1993))

You need only 5 of the 9 categories to win a playoff matchup. Even balanced teams end up giving up a category in the playoffs. Stream for the categories you can still win that week, not for raw volume in every category. ([09-23](https://youtu.be/C4vlgpJ62NI?t=454))
